title: 2016 AMC 12B Problem 17
statement: In \(\triangle ABC\) shown in the figure, \(AB=7,\) \(BC=8,\) \(CA=9,\) and \(\overline{AH}\) is an altitude. Points \(D\) and \(E\) lie on sides \(\overline{AC}\) and \(\overline{AB},\) respectively, so that \(\overline{BD}\) and \(\overline{CE}\) are angle bisectors, intersecting \(\overline{AH}\) at \(Q\) and \(P,\) respectively. What is \(PQ?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(x=BH.\) Then \(CH=8-x,\) and from the two right triangles \(AH^2=7^2-x^2=9^2-(8-x)^2.\) This gives \(x=2\) and \(AH=\sqrt{45}.\) By the angle bisector theorem in \(\triangle ACH,\) \(\dfrac{AP}{PH}=\dfrac{CA}{CH}=\dfrac96,\) so \(AP=\dfrac35 AH.\) Similarly in \(\triangle ABH,\) \(\dfrac{AQ}{QH}=\dfrac{BA}{BH}=\dfrac72,\) so \(AQ=\dfrac79 AH.\) Then \[ \begin{aligned} PQ &= AQ-AP \\ &= \left(\dfrac79-\dfrac35\right)AH \\ &= \dfrac{8}{45}\sqrt{45} \\ &= \dfrac{8}{15}\sqrt5. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: By the angle bisector theorem, \(\dfrac{AP}{PH}=\dfrac{CA}{CH}=\dfrac96\) and \(\dfrac{AQ}{QH}=\dfrac{BA}{BH}=\dfrac72;\) then \(PQ=AQ-AP\)
